subject: Logic
title: What Is Conditional Probability
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Is Conditional Probability.

hook.text: It's cloudy. Does that change the probability of rain? Of course—that's conditional probability.

buildup.text: P(A|B) means the probability of A given that B already happened. New information updates the odds.

discovery.text: P(rain|cloudy) is much higher than P(rain) alone. The condition narrows the sample space.

twist.text: P(A|B) is not the same as P(B|A). The probability of clouds given rain differs from rain given clouds.

climax.text: Conditional probability is how rational agents update beliefs when new evidence arrives.

quiz.question: What does P(A|B) represent?
options: Probability of A and B together
Probability of A given B happened
